info.title: Tiducto Transit API — Realtime
info.description: GTFS-RT live data (vehicles, trip updates, alerts), poll-based and key-authenticated. Companion to routing, stops and places; the four share one pack version. A member that has no value is absent, never null. A GTFS-RT enum value the decoder doesn't recognise is omitted. Every id in a response is feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`), exactly as routing's `gtfsId` and stop search return it, and an id in a request is used exactly as sent: a raw id, or one with another feed's prefix, is unknown. A query parameter not listed is a 400 `<name> is not allowed`, and a repeated one a 400 `<name> is invalid`. A method an operation doesn't take is a 405 `method_not_allowed`, `POST /realtime/v1/trip-updates` and `POST /realtime/v1/delays` included, and a path under `/realtime/v1/` that matches no operation is a 404 `not_found`. A response may come from a shared cache keyed by host, URL and `apikey`; such a response is not metered. Any other path that matches no operation, and every path of an environment without a realtime deployment, is the gateway's plain-text `404 Not Found`, outside every operation.

get.description:
Live vehicle positions for the given trips on one service date, at most one per trip run.
- A frequency-based trip (`frequencies.txt`) has several runs under one trip id, told apart by the feed's `start_time`: each run's vehicle is its own item, with its `startTime`, in order of `startTime` (a run without one first). `missing` lists the requested trip ids with no vehicle on any run.
- `serviceDate` is required: the GTFS service date, ISO-8601 `YYYY-MM-DD`, the same value a plan leg's, departure's or trip's `serviceDate` carries. Absent or empty is a 400 `serviceDate is required`, and a value that is not an ISO date a 400 `serviceDate is invalid`.
- A vehicle is returned only while it runs the trip on that service date, so a future date has none; each vehicle's `serviceDate` names the trip run it is on.
- `wheelchairAccessible`, `airConditioning`, `wifi` and `cardPayment` describe the vehicle the feed reports for the trip; each is absent when the feed doesn't say.
- `tripIds` is required: 1 to 50 comma-separated trip ids, each used exactly as sent and counted as sent. Absent or empty is a 400 `tripIds is required`, a blank entry (as in `1:39822,` or a space) a 400 `tripIds is invalid`, more than 50 a 400 `tripIds is out of range`.
- Ids are feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`), exactly as routing returns them; a raw id or another feed's id is unknown and listed in `missing`.
- A query parameter not listed is a 400 `<name> is not allowed`, and a repeated one a 400 `<name> is invalid`.
- The response carries `ETag`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<poll interval>, must-revalidate` and `Vary: apikey`; a request whose `If-None-Match` matches the `ETag` is a 304 without a body.

get.description:
Live vehicle for a single trip on one service date. Always 200 with a freshness envelope; `vehicle` is absent when none is currently reporting, a normal state, never a 404.
- `serviceDate` is required: the GTFS service date, ISO-8601 `YYYY-MM-DD`, the same value a plan leg's, departure's or trip's `serviceDate` carries. Absent or empty is a 400 `serviceDate is required`, and a value that is not an ISO date a 400 `serviceDate is invalid`.
- A vehicle is returned only while it runs the trip on that service date, so a future date has none; its `serviceDate` names the trip run it is on.
- `startTime` is optional: a GTFS time `H:MM:SS` or `HH:MM:SS`, hours up to 99, that selects the run of a frequency-based trip (`frequencies.txt`) the feed reports with that `start_time`, compared as a time (`8:10:00` is `08:10:00`). `vehicle` is absent when no run has it, and for a run the feed reports without a start time. Omitted, the answer is the trip's run with the earliest `startTime`, a run without one counting as earliest, so a trip that is not frequency-based answers as before. Empty counts as omitted, as for every parameter here; any other value not of that form is a 400 `startTime is invalid`.
- `wheelchairAccessible`, `airConditioning`, `wifi` and `cardPayment` describe the vehicle the feed reports for the trip; each is absent when the feed doesn't say.
- Ids are feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`), exactly as routing returns them; a raw id or another feed's id is unknown: `vehicle` is absent for it.
- A query parameter not listed is a 400 `<name> is not allowed`, and a repeated one a 400 `<name> is invalid`.
- The response carries `ETag`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<poll interval>, must-revalidate` and `Vary: apikey`; a request whose `If-None-Match` matches the `ETag` is a 304 without a body.

Absent or empty is a 400 `serviceDate is required`, and a value that is not an ISO date `serviceDate is invalid`.

Omitted or empty, the trip's run with the earliest `startTime` is answered, a run without one counting as earliest. Any other value not of that form is a 400 `startTime is invalid`.

get.description:
Live trip updates for trips on one service date, resolved per trip run (trip id + service date + the feed's start time): each run's schedule deviation, its GTFS-RT schedule relationship and its stop-time updates, and the trip modifications (detours) that select it. The successor of `GET /realtime/v1/delays`, with the same parameters and errors; its body lists the runs in `tripUpdates` (`delays` there), each with its `startTime` and `modifications`, and a trip with several runs has one item per run.
- A frequency-based trip (`frequencies.txt`) has several runs under one trip id, told apart by the feed's `start_time`: each live run is its own item, with its `startTime`, in order of `startTime` (a run without one first). `missing` lists the requested trip ids with no run.
- Trip modifications are experimental, as in GTFS-RT: a `TripModifications` entity applies to a trip run when its `selected_trips` name the trip and its `service_dates` hold the service date; one with `start_times` applies only to the runs whose `startTime` is one of them (never to a run without a `startTime`), one without to every run of the trip. A run that modifications select and no trip update reports is returned with empty `stopTimeUpdates`: one per listed start time without a reported run, or one without `startTime` when the trip has no run at all. Such a trip is not listed in `missing`.
- A replacement stop the feed defines as a realtime `Stop` entity carries its `name`, `latitude` and `longitude`; the modified trip's `shape` is the encoded polyline of the feed's `Shape` entity it names.
- `serviceDate` is the GTFS service date, ISO-8601 `YYYY-MM-DD`: the same value a plan leg's, departure's or trip's `serviceDate` carries. GTFS times may exceed 24:00, so a service date can differ from the departure's calendar date.
- `serviceDate` and `tripIds` are required; absent or empty is a 400 `<name> is required`.
- `tripIds` is 1 to 50 comma-separated trip ids, each used exactly as sent and counted as sent. A blank entry (as in `1:39822,` or a space) is a 400 `tripIds is invalid`, more than 50 a 400 `tripIds is out of range`.
- Ids are feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`), exactly as routing returns them; a raw id or another feed's id is unknown and listed in `missing`.
- A query parameter not listed is a 400 `<name> is not allowed`, and a repeated one a 400 `<name> is invalid`. Another method, `POST` included, is a 405 `method_not_allowed`.
- A trip instance the feed doesn't hold for that service date comes back in `missing`, never painted with another day's update.
- The response carries `ETag`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<poll interval>, must-revalidate` and `Vary: apikey`; a request whose `If-None-Match` matches the `ETag` is a 304 without a body.

apikey.name: apikey
apikey.description: The raw key in an `apikey` header (not Authorization: Bearer).

missing.description: Requested trip ids with no live vehicle on the requested service date, exactly as sent.

feedTimestamp.description: Epoch seconds of the feed's latest report; absent when the feed has not reported.

staleSeconds.description: Seconds since `feedTimestamp`, as of when this body was produced; a cached or revalidated body keeps that value, and the age now is the current time minus `feedTimestamp`. Absent when `feedTimestamp` is.

vehicle.description: The trip's live vehicle on the requested service date; absent when none is reporting, a normal state rather than an error.

feedTimestamp.description: Epoch seconds of the feed's latest report; absent when the feed has not reported.

staleSeconds.description: Seconds since `feedTimestamp`, as of when this body was produced; a cached or revalidated body keeps that value, and the age now is the current time minus `feedTimestamp`. Absent when `feedTimestamp` is.

Vehicle.description: A vehicle's live position and features, at most one per trip. A member the producer doesn't report is absent. `tripId`, `routeId`, `stopId` and `vehicleId` are feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`).

serviceDate.description: GTFS service date of the trip run the vehicle is on, ISO-8601 `YYYY-MM-DD`.

startTime.description: Start time of the trip run, as the feed's GTFS-RT `start_time` gives it: a GTFS time `HH:MM:SS` that may exceed `24:00:00`. It tells apart the runs of a frequency-based trip (`frequencies.txt`); absent when the feed gives none.

label.description: The vehicle's user-visible label, as the producer gives it.

timestamp.description: Epoch seconds of the position; absent when the producer doesn't report it.

wheelchairAccessible.description: GTFS-RT `VehicleDescriptor.WheelchairAccessible` of the vehicle reported for the trip; absent for `NO_VALUE`.

airConditioning.description: Whether the vehicle reported for the trip is air-conditioned; absent when unknown.

wifi.description: Whether the vehicle reported for the trip offers Wi-Fi; absent when unknown.

cardPayment.description: Whether the vehicle reported for the trip accepts card payment on board; absent when unknown.

TripUpdatesResponse.description: Trip updates and trip modifications for the requested service date. Feed freshness (`feedTimestamp`, `staleSeconds`) is global across the snapshot.

serviceDate.description: GTFS service date as ISO-8601 `YYYY-MM-DD`, echoing the request.

tripUpdates.description: One entry per requested trip with a live update or a trip modification on this service date.

missing.description: Requested trip ids with neither a live update nor a trip modification on this service date, exactly as sent.

feedTimestamp.description: Epoch seconds of the feed's latest report; absent when the feed has not reported.

staleSeconds.description: Seconds since `feedTimestamp`, as of when this body was produced; a cached or revalidated body keeps that value, and the age now is the current time minus `feedTimestamp`. Absent when `feedTimestamp` is.

DelaysResponse.description: Deprecated with `GET /realtime/v1/delays`; its successor `GET /realtime/v1/trip-updates` answers `TripUpdatesResponse`: this body with `delays` named `tripUpdates`, each trip also carrying its trip modifications. Delays for the requested service date. Feed freshness (`feedTimestamp`, `staleSeconds`) is global across the snapshot.

serviceDate.description: GTFS service date as ISO-8601 `YYYY-MM-DD`, echoing the request.

missing.description: Requested trip ids with no live delay on this service date, exactly as sent.

feedTimestamp.description: Epoch seconds of the feed's latest report; absent when the feed has not reported.

staleSeconds.description: Seconds since `feedTimestamp`, as of when this body was produced; a cached or revalidated body keeps that value, and the age now is the current time minus `feedTimestamp`. Absent when `feedTimestamp` is.

Delay.description: Live schedule deviation for one trip instance on the requested service date. `tripId` and `routeId` are feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`).

delaySeconds.description: Seconds, positive when late: the delay of the last stop-time update that carries one, its departure delay before its arrival delay. Absent when the updates give only absolute times.

stopTimeUpdates.description: Empty when the update has none.

TripUpdate.description: Live update for one trip run on the requested service date: its schedule deviation and the trip modifications (detours) that select it. A run with modifications and no GTFS-RT `TripUpdate` has empty `stopTimeUpdates` and no `delaySeconds`, `scheduleRelationship` or `routeId`. `tripId` and `routeId` are feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`).

startTime.description: Start time of the trip run, as the feed's GTFS-RT `start_time` (or `modified_trip.start_time`) gives it: a GTFS time `HH:MM:SS` that may exceed `24:00:00`. It tells apart the runs of a frequency-based trip (`frequencies.txt`), each its own item; absent when the feed gives none.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds, positive when late: the delay of the last stop-time update that carries one, its departure delay before its arrival delay. Absent when the updates give only absolute times.

stopTimeUpdates.description: Empty when the update has none. For a modified trip, as the feed reports them against the modified stop times.

modifications.description: Experimental, as GTFS-RT `TripModifications`. The modifications of every `TripModifications` entity whose `selected_trips` name this trip and whose `service_dates` hold the requested service date, and, when it has `start_times`, one of them is this run's `startTime`, in feed order; their delays accumulate along the trip. Absent when none applies.

TripModification.description: Experimental, as GTFS-RT `TripModifications.Modification`: a span of the trip's stop times replaced by `replacementStops`. A member the feed doesn't set is absent.

id.description: Feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`) id of the `FeedEntity` holding the `TripModifications`: a modified trip's `TripDescriptor.modified_trip.modifications_id`.

startTimes.description: The entity's `start_times`, GTFS times `HH:MM:SS` of a frequency-based trip: the modification applies only to the runs whose `startTime` is one of them, and never to a run without a `startTime`. Absent when it applies to every run of the trip on the service date.

startStop.description: The first original stop time replaced (`start_stop_selector`).

endStop.description: The last original stop time replaced, inclusive (`end_stop_selector`); absent when no stop time is replaced.

replacementStops.description: The stops the trip now visits in place of the replaced span, in order; empty when the feed lists none.

propagatedModificationDelay.description: Seconds added to every arrival and departure after the end of the modification; 0 when the feed doesn't set it.

alertId.description: Feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`) id of the `Alert` describing the modification (`service_alert_id`), as `GET /realtime/v1/alerts` returns it.

lastModifiedTime.description: Epoch seconds the modification last changed.

shape.description: The modified trip's path as an encoded polyline (Google's algorithm, 1e-5 precision), from the feed's `Shape` entity that the trip's `selected_trips.shape_id` names. Absent when the shape id names no `Shape` entity of the feed, e.g. a static `shapes.txt` shape.

StopSelector.description: Experimental, as GTFS-RT `StopSelector`: an original stop time of the trip, by `stopSequence` and/or `stopId` as the feed gives it. `stopId` is feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`).

ReplacementStop.description: Experimental, as GTFS-RT `ReplacementStop`. `stopId` is feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`). `name`, `latitude` and `longitude` are present only when the feed defines the stop as a realtime `Stop` entity; otherwise the stop is a static one, which the stop search returns.

travelTimeToStop.description: Seconds from the arrival at the reference stop, the stop before `startStop` (the trip's first stop when the modification starts there), to the arrival here.

StopTimeUpdate.description: `stopId` is feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`). A member the producer doesn't set is absent.

arrivalDelay.description: Seconds, positive when late; absent when the update gives only an absolute arrival time.

departureDelay.description: Seconds, positive when late; absent when the update gives only an absolute departure time.

AlertsResponse.description: The alerts active now across the environment's feeds: inside any of their active periods, or always for an alert without one.

feedTimestamp.description: Epoch seconds of the feed's latest report; absent when the feed has not reported.

staleSeconds.description: Seconds since `feedTimestamp`, as of when this body was produced; a cached or revalidated body keeps that value, and the age now is the current time minus `feedTimestamp`. Absent when `feedTimestamp` is.

Alert.description: A service alert. Each text is the producer's first translation. A member the producer doesn't set is absent. `id` is feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`).

activePeriods.description: Empty for an alert that is always active.

ActivePeriod.description: A period the alert is active in; an absent `start` or `end` leaves that side open.

InformedEntity.description: What the alert concerns. Every id here is feed-prefixed (`<feedId>:<id>`); one the producer doesn't set is absent.

ErrorResponse.description: Error body: a stable machine-readable `code`, which names a state, and a human-readable `message`.

code.description: One of `bad_request`, `key_missing`, `key_invalid`, `key_not_allowed`, `agreement_inactive`, `planning_limit_reached`, `not_found`, `method_not_allowed`, `length_required`, `payload_too_large`, `rate_limited`, `internal_error`, `upstream_unavailable`, `upstream_timeout`. New codes may be added.

message.description: For `bad_request`: `<field> is required|invalid|out of range|not allowed`, or `body is invalid` when the body is empty, not JSON or not an object.

field.description: Present only on a 400 that names one member: its dot path from the body root, array positions omitted, or the query parameter's name.
